comment: JetStore-owned. Reads a csv of text parts, calls the infer server's embeddings endpoint once per row, and writes the vector back onto the row. Registered as the Embed_Input_Parts process in jets/jets_init_db.sql against client JetsA and object type jetsa:EmbeddedData; see pipes_config/README.md for what that registration is and why a .pc.json alone does nothing. INPUT CONTRACT: the input file is a csv whose headers include part_key (a stable identifier for the row, used to key error reports) and part_text (the text to embed). The other headers are carried through untouched - the operator augments the record in place and does not project it. The three columns declared on the input_row channel below are ADDED to the file's own headers, which is how the operator can read the file directly with no staging pipe. OUTPUT: the augmented rows are written as csv under the JetStore stage prefix at process_name=Embed_Input_Parts/session_id=<id>/step_id=parts_embeddings/, and failures go to jetsapi.process_errors keyed by part_key.

cluster_config.comment: pool_size on the embed operator is a share of the infer server's budget rather than a throughput setting: the worker pool is built per node, so what the server sees is nodes x pool_size. Measured against nomic-embed-text on an L40S, throughput scales almost linearly to 16 concurrent and then stops, with only latency growing past it. default_max_concurrency 4 x pool_size 4 puts this pipeline exactly on that knee. Re-measure and re-divide if either the model or the card changes; 137M parameters is small enough that a larger embedding model will move the knee.

channels.comment: The input file's own columns are taken from the file, here adding the augmented columns only.
channels.name: input_row

apply.comment: vector_column is the whole configuration of the mapping: the vector lives at embeddings.0 and nowhere else, so the operator synthesizes that mapping and this file never names a response path. vector_as_rdf_type is deliberately unset, so the vector lands as json text - which is what a csv cell can carry, and what the object type's description promises. on_error is fail rather than the pass_through default: pass_through is right when an inference call augments a record that is useful without it, and wrong here, where a failed call writes the row out with an empty vector and the first consumer to notice is a similarity search returning slightly worse answers for ever.

output_mapping.comment: Provenance for the vector, and the reason to keep it: a vector is only comparable to other vectors from the same model, so a corpus that does not record which model produced each row cannot be re-embedded incrementally or audited after a model change. prompt_eval_count is the only token count an embeddings call produces.
